title: On Translating the letter for the old people
subtitle: 语言文化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 语言文化（人与社会·历史社会与文化·语言与文化）
meta: 主题语境：语言文化（人与社会·历史社会与文化·语言与文化）　|　核心词汇：translate　|　正文 350 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 translate 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1988 the postman ① translated the letter for the old people before dawn, and every sender in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the postman ② translates the letter for the old people in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ translate the letter for the old people at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ translated the letter for the old people before — a line in the list for June 1982 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Translating the letter for the old people before dawn, the postman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the envelope at the far box, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ translate the idea into daily practice in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Translate the idea into daily practice at once and never mention it again.

By 1995 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new sender from the next office ⑧ translates the idea into daily practice before dawn every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the box, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ translated the letter for the old people again when nobody else would.

⑩ To translate the letter for the old people, my mother said in 2000, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody translates the letter for the old people in public again and somebody must translate the letter for the old people before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 翻译（一般过去式 translated the letter for the old people：1988 年邮差头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 翻译（一般现在 translates the letter for the old people：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 翻译（不定式 to translate the letter for the old people：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 翻译（过去完成时 had translated the letter for the old people：1982 年六月的收发清单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 翻译（动名词 translating the letter for the old people 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 转化为（translate the idea into daily practice：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去转化为把这念头变成日日可行的做法）
G. v. 转化为（translate the idea into daily practice：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 翻译（后段两处：新来的寄信人照例 translates the idea into daily practice，而母亲又一次 translated the letter for the old people）

answers.why: translate 意为“翻译”，1988 年邮差天没亮就翻译为老人们翻那封信，那是邮局里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 translated。
translate 意为“翻译”，自那以后邮差当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 translates。
translate 意为“翻译”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯翻译为老人们翻那封信”，此处为不定式 to translate the letter for the old people。
translate 意为“翻译”，收发清单里 六月 那行字说明早在 1995 年之前就有人翻译过，故用过去完成时 had translated。
translate 意为“翻译”，邮差说“翻译为老人们翻那封信这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 translating the letter for the old people 作主语。
translate 意为“转化为”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去转化为把这念头变成日日可行的做法”，should ever 之后用原形 translate the idea into daily practice。
translate 意为“转化为”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻转化为把这念头变成日日可行的做法（translate the idea into daily practice at once），以后再也不要提起。
translate 意为“翻译”，新来的寄信人每个星期都照例转化为把这念头变成日日可行的做法，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 translates。
translate 意为“翻译”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就翻译为老人们翻那封信，用一般过去式 translated 叙述。
translate 意为“翻译”，结尾那句是母亲 2000 年的话：要翻译为老人们翻那封信，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和邮局记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 translate 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1988 the postman translated the letter for the old people before dawn, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the postman translates the letter for the old people in public whenever the office asks.
Translating the letter for the old people before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever translate the idea into daily practice in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new sender from the next office translates the idea into daily practice before dawn every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother translated the letter for the old people again, and the office remembered that half.
